title: SDK internal adoption retrospective and 10-day bootlog
content:
Purpose
---
This doc captures an internal adoption retrospective for the new SDK quick-onramp we shipped to a small cross-functional cohort (10 engineers across product, platform and solutions). It includes a 10-day log of what happened, liftable runbook items, observed friction, and proposed telemetry/contract changes before we promote the flow to broader developer audiences.

High-level objective
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-inference call from 45 minutes -> under 15 minutes for engineers unfamiliar with Redwood.
- Surface the earliest detectible failure modes so we can add guardrails to the public quickstart.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Wins: default auth and sample app pattern cut setup confusion; the interactive CLI stub produced immediate feedback for 7/10 participants.
- Pain: network proxy + corporate firewall issues blocked 2 participants for >1 day; clearer detection + fallback messages needed.
- Telemetry gaps: we had no way to link a participant's local run to the onboarding funnel; need ephemeral run ids tied into first 3 SDK calls.
- Next steps: a short implementation plan (see bottom) with three priorities: auth UX, network diagnostics, onboarding telemetry.

Cohort composition
- 10 internal participants: 4 product engineers, 3 infra/platform, 2 solutions engineers, 1 growth engineer testing sample integration scenarios.
- OS mix: Mac (8), Linux (2).
- Prior Redwood experience: 2 veterans, remainder novice.

10-day bootlog (annotated)
Day 0: prep
- Seeded repo with quickstart template: sample-app (Node/TS) + minimal serverless example. Added ephemeral API key generator endpoint for test accounts.
- Sent invites and a 20-min orientation doc.

Day 1: kickoff + first-run
- 7/10 completed first-run (npm install, set API_KEY, node sample.js) within 12–25 minutes.
- Notes: interactive CLI that verifies API key and pings /v1/models -> good signal.
- Blockers: corporate proxy detection failed for 2 participants (error: ECONNREFUSED).

Day 2: CLI improvements + FAQ patch
- Added clearer proxy error guidance (how to set HTTP_PROXY / socks5) and a test-helper command: rwi sdk diagnose-network.
- Observed: diagnose-network correctly surfaced TLS interception for 1 participant.

Day 3: sample prompts + telemetry trial
- Introduced 3 sample prompt templates: summarizer, extraction, chat-qa.
- Trial telemetry: local SDK emitted a short event to /internal/boot-events with boot_id. Privacy-safe (no prompt text). Mismatch: event arrived but could not be mapped to user due to missing run_id cookie.

Day 4: environment parity test
- Ran the sample-app under a container (alpine) to validate library binary dependencies. Two devs hit wasm fallback issues on older glibc. Added an alpine branch in CI.

Day 5: failure-mode rehearsal
- Simulated rate-limit errors and model-variant fallbacks. Noted that error messages were too terse — "rate_limited" with no 'retry-after' header in the client wrapper.
- Action: client wrapper updated to parse retry metadata from server and present human-friendly suggestion.

Day 6: SDK instrumentation review
- Telemetry events reviewed: install, first-auth-check, first-gen, first-error. Missing: sample_app_boot_sequence and model_selection_decision.

Day 7: cross-team demo + feedback
- Solutions engineers tried integrating the quickstart into a small chat widget. Integration took ~2 hours due to missing example of streaming tokens handling in the web widget sample.
- Added streaming example to the widget sample (on master).

Day 8: docs polish
- Rewrote quickstart to show a minimal curl example first, then full sample-app. This reduced initial confusion over environment variables.

Day 9: final run and survey
- 9/10 participants submitted survey. Aggregate ratings: ease-of-first-run 4.1/5, clarity 3.8/5, time-to-success median 18m.
- Major request: better local debugging tips (how to reproduce tokenization issues, inspect kv-cache, verbose logging flags).

Day 10: wrap-up + retrospective meeting
- Alignment on next steps, owners assigned. Agreed to a mini-release (v0.9.1) with auth UX + network diagnose + telemetry mapping.

Observed friction patterns (ranked)
1) Network / corporate proxy detection (critical): blocked full success for some users. Need programmatic detection + targeted help text and fallback paths (eg: redirect to a browser-based token exchange).
2) Auth confusion (medium): ephemeral API keys are helpful but the flow to create them should offer a one-click browser helper that sets a local env var or prints the export command.
3) Streaming integration examples (low-medium): web widget sample lacked token-by-token append pattern in README.
4) Error clarity (low): parse server retry metadata and show suggested actions.

Telemetry and contract proposals (concrete)
Goal: correlate onboarding funnel events with early SDK usage without capturing sensitive prompt content.
- Required events (privacy-safe): onboarding_boot_id (UUID), first_auth_success (boot_id, sdk_version, platform), first_generation_called (boot_id, model_name, response_time_ms, token_count_estimate), first_error (boot_id, error_code, http_status, is_retryable).
- Mapping requirement: UI quickstart should show an ephemeral boot_id on success and copy it to clipboard; users can paste it into support tickets. We can also offer opt-in collection of anonymous boot_ids via a consent prompt.
- Implementation note: events should send hashed machine_id (?) or ephemeral boot-only id, not persistent identifying info. Legal to review.

Actionable runbook items (MVP list)
- Priority P0 (owner: Diego)
  - Add rwi sdk diagnose-network command; include proxy/TLS MITM detection heuristics and common fixes text. (ETA 3 days)
  - Make quickstart print ephemeral boot_id and copy-to-clipboard on first successful auth. (ETA 2 days)
- Priority P1 (owner: Priya)
  - Add one-click browser flow to mint ephemeral API key and a small shell snippet to auto-export it. (ETA 5 days)
  - Add streaming token append example and minimal web widget integration guide. (ETA 6 days)
- Priority P2 (owner: Maya)
  - Add client-side parsing of retry metadata and better error messages. (ETA 7 days)
  - Instrument additional telemetry events (model_selection_decision, sample_app_boot_sequence). Check with security/legal on payloads. (ETA 7 days)

Open questions and risks
- Legal: do we need an explicit consent screen to collect ephemeral boot_ids from internal and external users? (task for security and legal)
- Telemetry storage: how long can we keep boot events? 30 days? 90 days? (ops cost + retention policy)
- Opt-in vs opt-out: early adopters found the boot_id useful—should it be opt-out or opt-in?

Suggested messaging for public quickstart (gist)
- "Try a single curl to see Redwood respond in under 10 seconds. If you hit a corporate proxy, run rwi sdk diagnose-network or follow the network troubleshooting link."
- Show ephemeral boot id copy button and a short paragraph explaining support usage.

Appendices
A. Quick commands used in cohort
- npm i @redwood/sdk
- npx rwi sdk init
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- node sample-app/index.mjs
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwi-base","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

B. Sample minimal telemetry schema (plaintext)
- onboarding_boot_id: UUIDv4
- event: first_auth_success
- sdk_version: semver
- client_platform: mac/linux/win
- model_name: string
- response_ms: integer

C. Survey highlights (verbatim excerpts)
- "Loved the CLI check. Saved me debugging time." — product eng
- "Proxy killed my day. We need a fallback that uses browser-based exchange." — infra
- "Streaming example would have helped the widget integration." — solutions

Next checkpoints
- Ship the P0 items within 1 week, follow up with a smaller cohort to validate network diagnostics fix.
- Re-run a 3-day micro-sprint for external beta customers after P1 shipped.

If you want to pair on execution, I can run the first support triage and collect sample boot_ids from the next cohort.

Maya
